title: Simulator Training:  Thunderstorm at Outdoor Concert

irb_consent.title: Training Information
text: This is a brief practice activity for learning how to use the simulator.

contact_screen.title: Contact Information
text: No contact information is collected during training.

scenario_description.title: How to Use the Simulator
text: This is a training to familiarize yourself with the Decision Making Simulator (DMS). The goal is to use this tool to study how people make decisions when facing unexpected and potentially threntening events.

Imagine that you are attending an outdoor community festival. A severe thunderstorm is approaching. You are facing the decision of staying at the concert and possibly exposing yourself to the thunderstorm, or to leaving early, missing some of the music at the concert.

During this scenario you are shown information tiles that cover information that may affect your decision to stay or to leave. After clicking on the tile, a window above the tiles will open and reveal this  information. After reviewing the information you have to close the window to proceed. Next you can either open another tile, or proceed to making your decision. Some of the information might be critical, other information might be irrelevant for your decision.

The scenarios will progress in timed steps by a certain amount of time (in this case 30 minutes) as indicated in the upper right corner by the advancing clock. By advancing to the next time step new information might become available to you to examine, and to base your decision on. It is important that you only open tiles that are important for your decision making. Ignore those tiles where you think that they will have no impact on your decision.

After reviewing all of the tiles that are containing important information, you can advance by selecting the "Go to Assessment" button at the bottom of the window. Two scales will be presented to you. You can select your level of concern and the likelihood that you will leave by clicking on the radio button that best indicates your assessment. Once you finished selecting both, you can advance to the decision screen by pressing "Continue to choice".

On this new screen you will see the options "LEAVE" and "STAY". If you select leave you will end this training scenario. If you select STAY, you will advance by one time step and new information may become available to you.

assessment_instructions: Use both sliders to show your judgment based on the information available in this practice step. Each slider ranges from 0 to 10 and begins at 5.

assessment_variables.prompt: How concerned are you about your safety right now?
How likely are you to leave the festival now?

decision_instructions: Select STOP if you would leave the festival now. Select NEXT STEP if you would continue monitoring the situation. The practice ends after Step 2 regardless of your choice.
completion_message: You have completed the practice activity. In the main scenario, review the information tiles, update the sliders, and choose whether to stop or continue when prompted.
